newsitem.title: USA: IES holders approve merger, reject MidAmerican bid.
newsitem.headline: IES holders approve merger, reject MidAmerican bid.

text.p: IES Industries Inc. said Thursday its shareholders approved a three-way merger with WPL Holdings Inc. and Interstate Power Corp. to form a new Midwest utility giant, Interstate Energy Corp.
In approving the complex, $2.25-billion merger, IES shareholders appeared to have rejected a rival, $1.17-billion bid from MidAmerican Energy Co. to acquire IES.
Des Moines-based MidAmerican disputed IES' preliminary tally of the shareholder vote, however, and said it would not concede its fight to acquire IES.
IES said more than 75 percent of IES shareholders voting, or more than 57 percent of shares outstanding, supported the three-way merger at a shareholder meeting here.

"We're not conceding that as the outcome," said MidAmerican Chief Executive Stanley Bright in a press conference following the meeting. "The outcome cannot be known until a final tally is completed and we will await that."
IES also said the three-way merger was approved by the shareholders of WPL, based in Madison, Wis., and Interstate Power, based in Dubuque, Iowa, at their respective shareholder meetings on Thursday.

"Given the progress we have already made, we expect to proceed with the remaining regulatory reviews and to close this merger in the next eight to 10 months," said Chief Executive Lee Liu of Cedar Rapids, Iowa-based IES.

Under terms of the merger agreement accepted Thursday, each IES share would be exchanged for 1.14 shares of the new company, each Interstate Power share would be exchanged for 1.11 shares of the new company and each WPL share would be exchanged on a one-for-one basis.
Based on Thursday's prices, each IES share would be worth $33.63 and each Interstate share would be worth $32.75.
IES shares were trading Thursday at $32.25, down 87.5 cents; Interstate was unchanged at $30.75, and WPL was trading at $29.50, down 25 cents, all on the New York Stock Exchange.
MidAmerican had offered IES shareholders a combination of stock and cash equivalent to $39 a share.

One analyst, who spoke on condition he not be identified, said the vote suggested shareholders felt the three-way merger would provide greater long term value than the higher-priced takeover by MidAmerican.
The final vote tally may be closer than IES' preliminary count, but it will not likely change the outcome, said Securities Corp. of Iowa utilities analyst John Curti.
"I don't know what MidAmerican can do ... It looks like the shareholders have spoken," Curti said.

MidAmerican is the largest electric power utility in Iowa. IES, WPL and Interstate Power are also electric utilities. Among them they provide electricity and natural gas to thousands of customers in Iowa, Minnesota, Illinois and Wisconsin.
"Interstate Energy Corporation will be a regional utility powerhouse, well positioned for the coming era of increased competition in our industry," Liu said.
